en.greeting: Hi! Today you'll learn to pass on what people said, even days later: with said and told, and with small changes to tenses, pronouns and time words. Let's go step by step.

steps.title: said or told?
steps.text: In A2 you passed on messages right away: *Sari says she's sick.* Now let's report what someone said earlier.
steps.body: When you report **later**, use the past: **said** or **told**. **tell** needs a **person** right after it: *She **told me** that…*, *He **told the team** that…*. **say** has no person after it: *She **said** that…* (or *said **to** me*). So *She said me…* ✗ and *He told that…* ✗. **that** can be left out. Indonesian *bilang* works for both, so look for the person.

steps.title: said and told in action
steps.text: Read these aloud. Look at what comes right after said and told.
steps.body: After **told** there's always a person (*me, the team, Pak Hasan*). After **said** there isn't, unless you add **to**. Notice the verbs after them are in the past too (*was*): that's the next step.

examples.en: Rina said that she was tired.
examples.id: Rina bilang bahwa dia capek.

examples.en: Rina told me that she was tired.
examples.id: Rina bilang ke aku bahwa dia capek.

examples.en: Pak Hasan told the team the client was happy.
examples.id: Pak Hasan memberi tahu tim bahwa kliennya senang.

examples.en: Budi said the KRL was very crowded.
examples.id: Budi bilang KRL-nya penuh sekali.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Sari asked her manager for a day off. Which word fits?

question.prompt: Yesterday Sari ___ her manager that she needed a day off.
question.explanation: A person (*her manager*) comes right after the gap, so use **tell → told**. *said her manager* is the classic mistake: **say** has no person after it. *say* is also not past.

steps.title: One step back
steps.text: Now the verb inside the message.
steps.body: On Monday Rina says: *'I **am** tired.'* A week later she's fine. If you say *Rina said she **is** tired*, it sounds like she's tired now. The words were said in the past, so the verb moves **one step back**: **am/is → was**, **are → were**, **work → worked**, **don't → didn't**, **will → would**, **can → could**, and past simple → **had + past participle** (*went → had gone*). Indonesian never changes the verb (*Dia bilang dia capek*), so this is easy to forget.

steps.title: Then and now
steps.text: See why the verb moves back.

timeline.title: Monday's words, reported a week later
timeline.caption: Rina spoke on Monday. By Tuesday she was fine. A week later you report her words in the past: she said she was tired.

steps.title: Reported a week later
steps.text: Here's what people said last week, reported today.
steps.body: If the person is talking to you **right now**, keep *says* and the present (*Rina says she's in the lobby*), like in A2. If it's **still true** (*He said the office opens at eight*), the present is fine too. But when you report **later** and it's over, move the verb back.

examples.en: Pak Hasan said he was in a meeting.
examples.id: Pak Hasan: 'Saya sedang rapat.' (am → was)

examples.en: The interns said they were hungry.
examples.id: Anak-anak magang: 'Kami lapar.' (are → were)

examples.en: Sari said she liked the new office.
examples.id: Sari: 'Saya suka kantor baru ini.' (like → liked)

examples.en: Budi said he would bring the projector.
examples.id: Budi: 'Saya akan bawa proyektornya.' (will → would)

examples.en: Bu Ani said she couldn't find her keys.
examples.id: Bu Ani: 'Saya tidak bisa menemukan kunci saya.' (can't → couldn't)

examples.en: Dimas said he had missed the bus.
examples.id: Dimas: 'Saya ketinggalan bus.' (missed → had missed)

steps.title: Move it back
steps.text: Rina couldn't meet Budi last Monday. Now Budi asks you why.

question.prompt: Last Monday Rina said: 'I don't have time today.' A week later you tell Budi: Rina said ___
options: she doesn't have time that day.
she didn't have time that day.
she didn't had time that day.
question.explanation: It was said a week ago, so **don't → didn't**. After *didn't* the verb stays in its base form: **didn't have**, not *didn't had*. *doesn't have* keeps the present, as if it were about now.

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Now a message in the past simple. Remember: past simple → had + past participle, and the words for people change too.

question.prompt: Last Friday Sari called, upset: 'My train left without me!' A week later you tell Emma. Arrange the words.
question.solution: Sari said her train had left without her.
question.explanation: The train left **before** Sari called, so the past simple moves back to **had left** (had + past participle). *my* and *me* become **her**, because you're talking about Sari.

steps.title: People, places and days
steps.text: Last thing: the small words for people, time and place.
steps.body: Use **your** point of view: **I → he/she**, **my → his/her**, **we → they**, **me → him/her**, and **you → me** if the message was for you. Time and place words change too: on Monday, *tomorrow* meant Tuesday, so a week later say **the next day**. **today → that day**, **yesterday → the day before**, **here → there**. *(A week later) She said she will come tomorrow* ✗ → *She said she **would** come **the next day***.

steps.title: Which day?
steps.text: Pak Hasan told you about a client meeting last month.

question.prompt: Last month Pak Hasan said: 'I met the client yesterday.' Today you report it: Pak Hasan said he had met the client ___
question.explanation: His *yesterday* was the day before he spoke, not your yesterday, so **yesterday → the day before**. *the next day* is for *tomorrow*.

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here's everything on one page. Keep it for later.

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · reported speech
artifact.intro: Reporting later: said or told, the verb one step back, and your own words for people, time and place.
rows: She said she would call me the next day.
will → would; you → me; tomorrow → the next day
She said she had lost her key the day before.
past → had + past participle; yesterday → the day before
He told me he was busy that day.
She said the food there was great.
tips: **tell + person** (told me, told us); **say** + no person (said that…, said to me…). *said me* ✗, *told that* ✗.
No change when you report **right away** with **says** (*She says she's tired*) or when it's **still true** (*He said the office opens at eight*).
Reported questions (*She asked where I lived*) and orders (*He told me to wait*) come in a later lesson.

examples.en: She told me that she was tired.
examples.id: Dia bilang ke aku bahwa dia capek.

examples.en: He said he would call me the next day.
examples.id: Dia bilang dia akan meneleponku keesokan harinya.

steps.title: Learn more
steps.text: Want more practice? Here's a video on said and told, and a page with exercises on reported statements.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kamu belajar menyampaikan ulang ucapan orang, bahkan beberapa hari kemudian: dengan said dan told, dan dengan sedikit perubahan pada tense, kata ganti dan keterangan waktu. Yuk, pelan-pelan saja.

steps.title: said atau told?
steps.text: Di A2 kamu menyampaikan pesan saat itu juga: *Sari says she's sick.* Sekarang kita laporkan apa yang dikatakan seseorang sebelumnya.
steps.body: Kalau kamu melapor **belakangan**, pakai bentuk lampau: **said** atau **told**. **tell** harus langsung diikuti **orang**: *She **told me** that…*, *He **told the team** that…*. **say** tidak diikuti orang: *She **said** that…* (atau *said **to** me*). Jadi *She said me…* ✗ dan *He told that…* ✗. **that** (= bahwa) boleh dihilangkan. *bilang* dalam bahasa Indonesia cocok untuk keduanya, jadi perhatikan ada orangnya atau tidak.

steps.title: said dan told dalam kalimat
steps.text: Baca keras-keras. Perhatikan apa yang datang tepat setelah said dan told.
steps.body: Setelah **told** selalu ada orang (*me, the team, Pak Hasan*). Setelah **said** tidak ada, kecuali kamu menambahkan **to**. Perhatikan juga, kata kerja setelahnya juga bentuk lampau (*was*): itu langkah berikutnya.

examples.en: Rina said that she was tired.
examples.id: Rina bilang bahwa dia capek.

examples.en: Rina told me that she was tired.
examples.id: Rina bilang ke aku bahwa dia capek.

examples.en: Pak Hasan told the team the client was happy.
examples.id: Pak Hasan memberi tahu tim bahwa kliennya senang.

examples.en: Budi said the KRL was very crowded.
examples.id: Budi bilang KRL-nya penuh sekali.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Sari minta cuti sehari ke manajernya. Kata mana yang cocok?

question.prompt: Lengkapi: Yesterday Sari ___ her manager that she needed a day off.
question.explanation: Ada orang (*her manager*) tepat setelah titik-titiknya, jadi pakai **tell → told**. *said her manager* adalah kesalahan klasik: **say** tidak diikuti orang. *say* juga bukan bentuk lampau.

steps.title: Mundur satu langkah
steps.text: Sekarang kata kerja di dalam pesannya.
steps.body: Hari Senin Rina bilang: *'I **am** tired.'* Seminggu kemudian dia sudah sehat. Kalau kamu bilang *Rina said she **is** tired*, kedengarannya dia capek sekarang. Kata-katanya diucapkan di masa lalu, jadi kata kerjanya **mundur satu langkah**: **am/is → was**, **are → were**, **work → worked**, **don't → didn't**, **will → would**, **can → could**, dan past simple → **had + past participle** (*went → had gone*). Bahasa Indonesia tidak pernah mengubah kata kerjanya (*Dia bilang dia capek*), jadi ini gampang terlupa.

steps.title: Dulu dan sekarang
steps.text: Lihat kenapa kata kerjanya mundur.

timeline.title: Ucapan hari Senin, dilaporkan seminggu kemudian
timeline.caption: Rina bicara hari Senin. Hari Selasa dia sudah sehat. Seminggu kemudian kamu melaporkan ucapannya dalam bentuk lampau: she said she was tired.

steps.title: Dilaporkan seminggu kemudian
steps.text: Ini ucapan orang-orang minggu lalu, dilaporkan hari ini.
steps.body: Kalau orangnya bicara kepadamu **saat ini juga**, tetap pakai *says* dan bentuk sekarang (*Rina says she's in the lobby*), seperti di A2. Kalau **masih benar** (*He said the office opens at eight*), bentuk sekarang juga boleh. Tapi kalau kamu melapor **belakangan** dan situasinya sudah lewat, mundurkan kata kerjanya.

examples.en: Pak Hasan said he was in a meeting.
examples.id: Pak Hasan: 'Saya sedang rapat.' (am → was)

examples.en: The interns said they were hungry.
examples.id: Anak-anak magang: 'Kami lapar.' (are → were)

examples.en: Sari said she liked the new office.
examples.id: Sari: 'Saya suka kantor baru ini.' (like → liked)

examples.en: Budi said he would bring the projector.
examples.id: Budi: 'Saya akan bawa proyektornya.' (will → would)

examples.en: Bu Ani said she couldn't find her keys.
examples.id: Bu Ani: 'Saya tidak bisa menemukan kunci saya.' (can't → couldn't)

examples.en: Dimas said he had missed the bus.
examples.id: Dimas: 'Saya ketinggalan bus.' (missed → had missed)

steps.title: Mundurkan
steps.text: Rina tidak bisa bertemu Budi Senin lalu. Sekarang Budi bertanya kenapa.

question.prompt: Senin lalu Rina bilang: 'I don't have time today.' Seminggu kemudian kamu bilang ke Budi: Rina said ___
options: she doesn't have time that day.
she didn't have time that day.
she didn't had time that day.
question.explanation: Ucapannya seminggu lalu, jadi **don't → didn't**. Setelah *didn't*, kata kerjanya tetap bentuk dasar: **didn't have**, bukan *didn't had*. *doesn't have* tetap bentuk sekarang, seolah-olah tentang saat ini.

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Sekarang pesan dalam past simple. Ingat: past simple → had + past participle, dan kata untuk orangnya juga berubah.

question.prompt: Jumat lalu Sari menelepon dengan kesal: 'My train left without me!' Seminggu kemudian kamu cerita ke Emma. Susun kata-katanya.
question.solution: Sari said her train had left without her.
question.explanation: Keretanya berangkat **sebelum** Sari menelepon, jadi past simple mundur menjadi **had left** (had + past participle). *my* dan *me* menjadi **her**, karena kamu sedang membicarakan Sari.

steps.title: Orang, tempat dan hari
steps.text: Terakhir: kata-kata kecil untuk orang, waktu dan tempat.
steps.body: Pakai sudut pandang **kamu**: **I → he/she**, **my → his/her**, **we → they**, **me → him/her**, dan **you → me** kalau pesannya untukmu. Keterangan waktu dan tempat juga berubah: hari Senin, *tomorrow* berarti Selasa, jadi seminggu kemudian bilang **the next day**. **today → that day**, **yesterday → the day before**, **here → there**. *(Seminggu kemudian) She said she will come tomorrow* ✗ → *She said she **would** come **the next day***.

steps.title: Hari yang mana?
steps.text: Bulan lalu Pak Hasan cerita tentang rapat dengan klien.

question.prompt: Bulan lalu Pak Hasan bilang: 'I met the client yesterday.' Hari ini kamu melaporkannya: Pak Hasan said he had met the client ___
question.explanation: *Yesterday* menurut Pak Hasan adalah sehari sebelum dia bicara, bukan kemarin menurutmu, jadi **yesterday → the day before**. *the next day* untuk *tomorrow*.

steps.title: Ringkasan
steps.text: Ini semuanya dalam satu halaman. Simpan untuk nanti.

artifact.title: Ringkasan · reported speech
artifact.intro: Melapor belakangan: said atau told, kata kerja mundur satu langkah, dan kata-katamu sendiri untuk orang, waktu dan tempat.
rows: She said she would call me the next day.
will → would; you → me; tomorrow → the next day
She said she had lost her key the day before.
past → had + past participle; yesterday → the day before
He told me he was busy that day.
She said the food there was great.
tips: **tell + orang** (told me, told us); **say** + tanpa orang (said that…, said to me…). *said me* ✗, *told that* ✗.
Tidak berubah kalau kamu melapor **saat itu juga** dengan **says** (*She says she's tired*) atau kalau **masih benar** (*He said the office opens at eight*).
Pertanyaan yang dilaporkan (*She asked where I lived*) dan perintah (*He told me to wait*) dibahas di pelajaran berikutnya.

examples.en: She told me that she was tired.
examples.id: Dia bilang ke aku bahwa dia capek.

examples.id: Dia bilang dia akan meneleponku keesokan harinya.
